investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC via curl (plain HTTP GET, -L to follow redirects, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser): retained the homepage (www.volksbuehne.berlin redirects to the canonical www.volksbuehne-berlin.de), the /en/konzerte/ (Concerts) listing page, the site's own public sitemap.xml, and 3 independent production/event detail pages -- including one explicitly at 'Roter Salon', this investigation's specific target sub-venue.

probe_history.reason: The venue's own homepage already links directly to individual dated performance pages at a self-describing URL pattern (/en/productions/{slug}/{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}/). The site's own public sitemap.xml (179,761 bytes, plain static XML, no auth) confirms comprehensive static discovery: 92 of its URLs match the dated-performance pattern (.../produktionen/{slug}/{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}/) out of 263 total production-related URLs. Three independently sampled event detail pages (House of Hopes on the Main Stage, Heith und Tarawansawelas: Duori at Roter Salon, Space Afrika present: Quiet Storm at Vorbühne) each server-render one application/ld+json schema.org Event-family block (DanceEvent/MusicEvent) with a full UTC-offset-qualified startDate/endDate, a self-referencing canonical 'url', a named location (sometimes with a full PostalAddress, sometimes name-only), and an organizer. This fully answers the investigation at Level 1 -- no escalation needed.

venue_reference: Volksbühne am Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz, including its attached concert halls Roter Salon and Grüner Salon (theatre + concert venue, Linienstraße 227, Mitte, Berlin)

identity.notes: www.volksbuehne.berlin (the domain initially discovered via search) HTTP-redirects (301, then a further internal redirect) to https://www.volksbuehne-berlin.de/en/, which is the domain actually served -- both are treated as the same official identity. Every retained event's own JSON-LD 'organizer' ('Volksbühne Berlin', url https://www.volksbuehne-berlin.de/) and 'location.address' (Linienstraße 227, 10178 Berlin, DE for the Main Stage sample) directly confirm official identity and match the venue's well-known Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz address. 'Roter Salon' itself appears as a JSON-LD location.name on a real sampled event, directly confirming it is this same organisation's own attached concert hall, not a separate entity.

site_classification.platform: Custom-built bilingual (DE/EN) site (no CMS generator meta found). Each individual production/performance page (both the German /produktionen/ and English /en/productions/ paths) server-renders one schema.org Event-family application/ld+json block. Ticketing is embedded via ticket.volksbuehne-berlin.de, an Eventim-powered webshop that is this venue's OWN first-party ticket shop (not a third-party listings aggregator) -- referenced as each JSON-LD 'offers[].url'.

title.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'name' field. Value shown is from the Roter Salon sample (this investigation's specific target sub-venue).

start_date.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'startDate', a full ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset (+02:00, CEST) -- confirmed consistent across all 3 sampled pages. Value shown is from the Roter Salon sample.

time.notes: Time-of-day + offset portion of the same JSON-LD 'startDate'.

end.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'endDate', consistently a genuinely distinct value from startDate on all 3 sampled pages (a real 2-3 hour duration each time, unlike HKW's occasional startDate==endDate pattern seen in a separate investigation).

venue_location.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'location.name'. A full PostalAddress is present for some records (e.g. the Main Stage sample: Linienstraße 227, 10178 Berlin, DE) but not others (Roter Salon and Vorbühne samples carry only location.name, no address) -- honest per-record variability, all still naming one of Volksbühne's own internal spaces within its single Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz building.

source_record_id.notes: No separate 'identifier'/'@id' field exists in the JSON-LD, but each event page's own JSON-LD 'url' field is a self-referencing canonical URL (confirmed identical to the page actually fetched, and matching this venue's own sitemap.xml <loc> entry) -- one URL per specific performance date/time (the date+time is even encoded directly in the URL's own path segment, e.g. '20261009-1800'), so unlike Radialsystem's one-slug-many-dates situation, this source's own URL is already unique per occurrence.

event_url.notes: Each event page's own JSON-LD 'url' field, self-referencing and canonical.

price.notes: No literal numeric price value was found in any of the 3 sampled pages. One sample (House of Hopes) carries a JSON-LD 'offers' array with 'url'/'availability'/'priceCurrency' but no 'price' number (all 3 offers were SoldOut); the other two samples carry no 'offers' field at all.

blockers.description: The sitemap.xml mixes non-performance production pages (season overview pages, 'pressematerial' press-kit pages) alongside genuine dated performance pages; a collector should filter to URLs matching the .../{slug}/{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}/ pattern (92 of 263 production-related URLs matched this in the retained sample) rather than fetching every production-related URL.

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from the venue's own retained JSON-LD organizer/location data, with Roter Salon itself confirmed as this organisation's own location on a real sampled event.
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved, supported class, reached entirely at Level 1.

A CONFIRMED public data path retained for both the sitemap.xml discovery mechanism and the event detail page JSON-LD, with 3 independently real sampled events across 3 different rooms (Main Stage, Roter Salon, Vorbühne).
title, start_date, time, end, venue_location, source_record_id, and event_url all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
price honestly NOT_PRESENT (no literal numeric value in any sample) -- no fields fabricated.
recommended_family JSON_LD, this project's own existing, already-proven generic family -- requires no new code family.
